fields.title: Nothing checks that a .NET build collects coverage

sections.What it checks:
* [std-NETTST.coverage-is-collected-by-the-build](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/297de4eed28ec0ed420ceb18c1b890124924676e/examples/engineering/standards/platform/dotnet/testing.md#coverage-is-collected-by-the-build) says a build "**MUST** collect coverage from its test run and publish
  the report".
* It says a build "**SHOULD** write the report in Cobertura format: with `--collect:"XPlat Code Coverage"` under
  VSTest, or with `--coverage --coverage-output-format cobertura` under Microsoft.Testing.Platform, with
  `Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.CodeCoverage` referenced".
sections.How it works:
Nothing runs. The check this rule needs is a pipeline step after `dotnet test`. It fails where the run wrote no Cobertura report:

```sh
find . -path '*/TestResults/*' -name '*cobertura.xml' | grep -q .
```

The search matches both forms the `SHOULD` names. VSTest writes `TestResults/<guid>/coverage.cobertura.xml`, and Microsoft.Testing.Platform writes `TestResults/<guid>.cobertura.xml`. A build using another collector, as the `SHOULD` allows, changes the path the step searches for.

The step has to come from a shared pipeline template that branch policy requires. A team writing its own pipeline leaves out the step along with the collector. A pre-commit check or a Claude Code hook sees the pipeline definition, and could only search it for the collector flag.
sections.Coverage and gaps:
A reviewer reading the pipeline definition is the only thing that notices a missing collector today.

The check proves a report was written. It does not prove the report was published, or that each test project is excluded from its own figure.
